title: do i have endometriosis? we're going to try and find out... without surgery

segments.text: This blood test might diagnose my endometriosis without having to get surgery. I have suspected endometriosis. I've had that for about 7 years, which is extremely common among women. They go through 7 to 10 years before getting diagnosed. I also have had a transvaginal ultrasound. It came back clear. I had a pelvic MRI. It came back clear. Really common among women.

Imaging modalities just don't pick up endo. Only option left for a lot of women is to get surgery, which is invasive. It's also costly. And so [music] we're testing what can you do without surgery? So this is Frontier Science right here. Let's see if we can figure out do I have endometriosis or not.

>> Ben, to make this understandable, imagine you have an alien that's growing inside you. It hurts. You don't know if you have or not. You get imaging, they're like, "Well, it doesn't look like you have an alien." But you still feel the pain. So this is basically allowing Kate to say does she have that growing inside of her? If she does, then there's potentially non-invasive ways to deal with this. So today we're trying to eliminate the surgery of having to open her up to see is the alien inside? And so it's really cool. The science just got out there. We're one of the first to try it, and we're very excited to see if this can pick up what imaging could not.
